candidate.answerReason: The figure contains five full-face joins. Six separate unit cubes have total surface area 36 square inches, and each join hides two unit faces, leaving 36 − 10 = 26.

methods.label: Remove the faces hidden at joins
methods.explanation:
Start by imagining the six cubes separated. Each cube has six faces, each with area \(1\cdot1=1\) square inch, so their combined surface area is \(6\cdot6=36\) square inches.

Now count the places where whole faces meet in the drawing. There are two joins within the central stack of three cubes, one join attaching the cube on the right, and two joins along the lower chain extending toward the left. These are all five full-face joins. A contact only along an edge hides no face area.

Each full-face join hides one face from each of its two cubes, so it removes two square inches. Every face is either exposed or belongs to exactly one such join. Therefore the total surface area, including the bottom and the unseen sides, is
\[
36-2\cdot5=\boxed{26}
\]
square inches, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method derives the surface count from six faces per cube and ordinary whole-number arithmetic.

methods.label: Count faces in each direction
methods.explanation:
Each exposed face is a square inch. To include every face exactly once, count the faces pointing in the six possible directions: up, down, and the four horizontal directions.

There are four vertical columns: the central column of height three and three columns of height one. Each column has one exposed top face and one exposed bottom face, giving \(4+4=8\) square inches.

Next look along the horizontal direction from the central stack toward the cube attached on its right. In this direction the cubes form five separate rows: one row contains the middle cube and its right neighbor, and the other four cubes each occupy a row of their own. Each row has an exposed face at each end, giving \(5+5=10\) square inches.

In the remaining horizontal direction, the bottom chain forms one row of three cubes. The two higher cubes in the central stack and the right-hand cube each form a separate row. These four rows contribute \(4+4=8\) square inches at their ends.

All these rows are unbroken, so their end faces account for all exposed faces in the corresponding directions. The total is
\[
8+10+8=\boxed{26}
\]
square inches, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: This is an elementary spatial counting method using rows and columns of cubes, with no formal three-dimensional coordinates.

The catalog's rectangular-prism surface-area nodes do not cover that target, so they are not assigned as assessed knowledge. Cube faces and square area support both methods. Mixed integer arithmetic is local to the cancellation method, while viewing objects from different directions supports the directional method. The proposed missing node names the actual task without assigning an unsupported equivalence or implying mastery.

needsNewNodes.name: Exterior surface area of assemblies of unit cubes
needsNewNodes.description: Determine the exterior surface area of a specified assembly of face-aligned unit cubes by counting exposed unit faces, including unseen faces. Distinguish full-face joins from edge or vertex contacts, and justify that every exterior face is counted once.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog covers cube and rectangular-prism surface areas, square area, and recognizing component solids, but lacks a specific target for exposed surface area of an irregular cube assembly.

review.mathematicalCheck: The drawing has five full-face joins: two in the vertical stack, one to the right, and two along the lower chain. Thus 36-2(5)=26. Directional counting independently gives four vertical columns, five rows in one horizontal direction, and four in the other, totaling 8+10+8=26. Each row is contiguous, so its two ends count all exterior faces in that direction.
review.levelCheck: Both methods use elementary spatial reasoning, square area, and whole-number arithmetic appropriate for AMC 8.
review.methodDistinctness: Removing internal face pairs and enumerating exterior faces by direction offer distinct counting ideas.
review.annotationCheck: Shared cube and square-area support is justified; arithmetic and directional viewing remain method-local. Leaving assessedIds empty and proposing an assembly-surface-area node honestly respects the narrower existing surface-area scopes.
